name: Ciprofloxacin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Ciprofloxacin is partly cleared by the liver and gut, so kidney impairment changes its levels less than for many antibiotics. The US labels still lower the dose at creatinine clearance (CrCl) 50 mL/min or less (oral) or below 30 mL/min (intravenous, IV) and dose after dialysis. Oral and IV doses differ; do not transpose oral mg values to IV.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault).

bands.recommendation: Oral: CrCl >50, usual dosing; CrCl 30–50, 250 to 500 mg every 12 hours (label). IV: CrCl >30, usual dose (IV label).

Oral: CrCl 5–29, 250 to 500 mg every 18 hours (label); severe infection: a 750 mg unit dose may be given at these intervals with careful monitoring. IV: CrCl 5–29, 200 to 400 mg every 18 to 24 hours (IV label).
Oral: CrCl 5–29, 250 to 500 mg every 18 hours (label). IV: CrCl 5–29, 200 to 400 mg every 18 to 24 hours (IV label). Below 5 not on dialysis: not addressed; specialist input.

hd.text: Oral: 250 to 500 mg every 24 hours, after dialysis (label). IV: dialysis not addressed in the IV label; specialist input.

pd.text: Oral: 250 to 500 mg every 24 hours (the label groups hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis). IV: dialysis not addressed in the IV label; specialist input. For PD-associated peritonitis (ISPD 2022): intraperitoneal continuous maintenance 50 mg/L (no intermittent IP data); systemic oral 500–750 mg daily (750 mg twice daily for CCPD) (ISPD Table 6).

crrt.text: Not in label. Published CRRT regimens: 200–400 mg IV every 8–12 hours by effluent rate (Li 2020); specialist input.

dialyzable: Minimal: less than 10% removed by hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis (label).
monitoring: Tendon rupture, QT prolongation, dysglycemia, central nervous system effects; crystalluria (keep hydrated).

pediatric.approved_ages: Complicated urinary tract infection (cUTI) and pyelonephritis: 1 to 17 years. Inhalational anthrax and plague: birth to 17 years. Not a drug of first choice in children (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: cUTI/pyelonephritis: 10 to 20 mg/kg every 12 hours. Anthrax: 15 mg/kg every 12 hours. Plague: 15 mg/kg every 8 to 12 hours (oral, label).
pediatric.max_dose: cUTI: 750 mg per dose, even above 51 kg. Anthrax and plague: 500 mg per dose (label).

renal.recommendation: No information for CrCl <50 mL/min/1.73 m2 in children (excluded from trials) (label). Specialist input.

pediatric.neonates: Neonates: anthrax and plague indications start from birth at 15 mg/kg; no neonatal kidney guidance. Specialist input.
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

pediatric: The 50–59 part of our 30–59 band falls in 'usual dosing' for children; label threshold is CrCl <50 mL/min/1.73 m2.
